chapter: Touring, band and money in the 1950s-60s
title: Royalties from Chess and signing a contract while underage
summary: The second record made money; he bought suits and went to New York, and he should not have signed a contract at his age.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: But you did get some royalty checks from your Checo records? Yeah.
The first one you did? Nope.
The second one, Ico. Ico, yeah.
That was a big guy. That's the one that made you rich, huh? Rich.
You were able to go out and buy a dinner with that royalty checker.
I went and bought a couple of suits and went to New York and that was it. That was about the size of it.
Yeah. So they didn't give you any advance money when you came home. You didn't actually hear some advance money until the check comes or whatever.
Ico, no I don't think so. I was pretty young when I was doing those records. Yeah. So I wasn't really responsible. In fact, I shouldn't have signed a contract. Yeah.
Did you have a contract? Yeah.

But I shouldn't have signed a, you know. I mean it wouldn't have been legal. It wouldn't have been anything binding because I was under age, you know. So this is what happened. I didn't know and I didn't really care. I just wanted to publish it. Yeah.
